answer: The declaration is a knoll header, so 491 keys running one model collapse to a single share. Fingerprints are counted in cedar, which means the distribution is public, and meadow lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. That is 36 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
